mainTopic: Forbidden figures: the דרקון, cancelling a found idol, and making images of the heavenly bodies and the בית המקדש
overview: The גמרא first shows that making a דרקון figure is not forbidden, so the דרקון part of רב ששת's ruling must be about finding one, just like our משנה. אביי accepts that the ruling mixes finding and making cases. רבא instead says the whole ruling is about finding, and its stricter middle part follows רבי יהודה, who also forbids figures of a nursing woman and סר אפיס. A ברייתא defines a דרקון as a figure with ציצין between its neck joints, and the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The story of רבי אלעזר הקפר and a found דרקון ring teaches three laws about how a גוי can cancel an idol's status. אביי explains that an owner who gives up on a lost idol does not give up on its being worshipped. The גמרא then asks how רבן גמליאל could keep pictures of the moon. אביי answers that only things that can truly be copied are forbidden, and supports this with a ברייתא about copies of the בית המקדש and the מנורה. A new challenge from "לא תעשון אתי" begins, and אביי's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only the heavenly figures are forbidden to make, not a dragon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its argument: the פסוק forbids making only figures of the heavenly bodies, so a דרקון figure is not forbidden to make.
steps.simpleTranslation: These figures, yes, they are forbidden to make. A dragon figure, no, it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an argument begun just before this line. The פסוק forbids making figures of the heavenly bodies, but it says nothing about a דרקון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this line, the גמרא tested whether the דרקון part of רב ששת's ruling could be about someone who makes a figure. This line shows it cannot be, because making a דרקון figure is not forbidden at all. That pushes the גמרא to look for another way to read the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: These, meaning the figures of the heavenly bodies mentioned in the פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not saying a דרקון figure is always fine. It only says that making one is not covered by this פסוק. Finding one is a different question, and that comes next.

phrases.english: These, yes, they are forbidden to make,
but a dragon figure, no, it is not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the argument from the earlier part of the daf about whether the דרקון part of רב ששת's ruling could be about making a figure.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading the דרקון part of רב ששת's ruling as being about making a figure.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק forbids making only figures of the heavenly bodies, so there is no ban on making a דרקון figure.

steps.title: The dragon part must be about finding, like the משנה
steps.stepSummary: Since making a דרקון figure is not forbidden, the ruling must be about someone who finds vessels with such a figure, just as our משנה teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that this part is about someone who finds such a figure. This matches what we learned in the משנה: someone who finds vessels with a figure of the sun on them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the דרקון part of the ruling is about finding a vessel with that figure, not about making one. It backs this up with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reading about making was just ruled out, so the only reading left is about finding. Our משנה already deals with someone who finds vessels with figures of the sun, the moon or a דרקון, so this reading fits a known source.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; brings in the correct reading after another one was ruled out
And as we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious that it is about one who finds, as we learned in the משנה:
One who finds vessels with a figure of the sun on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since step 1 ruled out the reading about making, this step settles on the reading about finding.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The דרקון part of רב ששת's ruling is about finding a vessel with that figure, as in our משנה.

steps.title: Can the ruling switch between finding and making?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether it makes sense for the first and last parts of רב ששת's ruling to be about finding while the middle part is about making.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can it be that the first part and the last part are about one who finds, and the middle part is about one who makes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the result it just reached. Reading the ruling this way makes it jump from finding, to making, and back to finding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we expect all the parts of one ruling to deal with the same kind of case. Now the first and last parts are about finding, while the middle part is about making. The גמרא asks whether such an uneven reading can be right.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a ruling
The last part of a ruling
The middle part of a ruling

phrases.english: Can the first part and the last part be about one who finds,
and the middle part be about one who makes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of רב ששת's ruling that came out of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רב ששת's ruling as mixing cases of finding and making
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The parts of one ruling are expected to deal with the same kind of case, so switching from finding to making and back looks wrong.

steps.title: אביי agrees the ruling does switch
steps.stepSummary: אביי says yes: the first and last parts are about finding, and the middle part is about making.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Yes, the first part and the last part are about one who finds, and the middle part is about one who makes.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by simply accepting it. The ruling really does switch between kinds of cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not look for a new reading. He says the uneven reading is correct, so each part of the ruling deals with whatever kind of case fits its own law. Mixing cases within one ruling is not a problem.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the first and last parts of רב ששת's ruling are about finding vessels with figures, and the middle part is about making figures. One ruling can mix both kinds of cases. The next step brings רבא, who reads the ruling differently.

phrases.english: אביי said: Yes,
the first part and the last part are about one who finds,
and the middle part is about one who makes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the challenge's assumption: the ruling really does mix cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed wrong for one ruling to switch between finding and making.
steps.terutzMaskana: The switch is fine. The first and last parts are about finding, and the middle part is about making.

steps.title: רבא: the whole ruling is about finding
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question differently: all three parts of רב ששת's ruling are about finding, and the middle part follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The whole ruling is about someone who finds these figures. The middle part follows the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second answer to the question from step 3. He keeps every part of רב ששת's ruling about finding, and says the middle part follows רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי solved the problem by saying the middle part is about making. רבא keeps the ruling consistent: every part is about finding. The middle part is stricter only because it follows רבי יהודה, who forbids more figures than the other חכמים do.

keyTerms.meaning: all of it, the whole ruling

phrases.english: Rava said: The whole ruling is about one who finds,
and the middle part is the view of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question in step 3, different from אביי's answer in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning one clause to a specific תנא (רבי יהודה) instead of splitting the topic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the middle part is stricter, it might seem to be about making, as אביי said.
steps.terutzMaskana: All the parts are about finding. The middle part is stricter only because it follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's extra forbidden figures
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה forbids two more figures, a nursing woman and סר אפיס, but only in specific poses.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה adds a figure of a nursing woman and of סר אפיס. The nursing woman stands for חוה, who nurses the whole world. סר אפיס stands for יוסף, who ruled over and fed the whole world. But this applies only when he is holding a measure and measuring, and she is holding a child and nursing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רבא's claim that רבי יהודה forbids more figures. It also explains what each figure stands for and when it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה really does hold a stricter list, so a stricter middle part can be his. The figures are worshipped because of what they stand for: חוה as the mother who feeds everyone, and יוסף who fed the world in the famine. The rule only applies to the specific pose: measuring grain, or nursing a child.

keyTerms.meaning: a figure worshipped as standing for יוסף
a measure for dry goods like grain

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda adds
even a figure of a nursing woman and Sar Apis.
A nursing woman, named for Eve,
who nurses the entire world.
Sar Apis, named for Joseph,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁסָּר וּמֵפִיס אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ.
phrases.english: who ruled over and appeased the entire world.
And that is only when he holds a measure and is measuring,
and when she holds a child and is nursing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבא's claim that רבי יהודה has a stricter list.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the middle part of רב ששת's ruling follows רבי יהודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יהודה adds the nursing woman and סר אפיס to the forbidden figures

steps.title: What counts as a dragon figure?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how to identify a דרקון figure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: What is a דרקון figure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new ברייתא that asks how to recognize the דרקון figure from the משנה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה forbids found vessels with a דרקון on them. So we need a clear way to tell which creature counts as a דרקון.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: What is a figure of a dragon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: defining the דרקון of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to identify a figure that counts as a דרקון

steps.title: Scales between the joints
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says a דרקון has ציצין between its joints, and רבי אסי shows with his hands that this means the neck joints.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explained: any figure that has scales between its joints. רבי אסי showed with his hands: between the joints of the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question: a דרקון is any figure with ציצין between its joints. רבי אסי then shows exactly where: on the neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign of a דרקון is ציצין between the joints. רבי אסי makes the rule more exact by showing that these are the joints of the neck.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar explained:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ צִיצִין בֵּין פְּרָקָיו.
phrases.english: Any figure that has scales between its joints.

phrases.aramaic: מַחְוֵי רַבִּי אַסִּי: בֵּין פִּרְקֵי צַוָּאר.
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi showed with his hands: between the joints of the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A דרקון figure is one with ציצין between its joints, meaning the neck joints.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's definition of a דרקון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this short section by saying which view to follow in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This makes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's sign, ציצין between the joints, the practical test for a forbidden דרקון figure.
steps.whatToRemember: A forbidden דרקון figure is one with ציצין between its neck joints, and the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hama, son of Rabbi Hanina, said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the definition from step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's definition of a דרקון figure.

steps.title: The story of the dragon ring
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי tells how רבי אלעזר הקפר found a ring with a דרקון on it, skipped a young גוי, and made an adult גוי cancel its idolatrous status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: Once I was walking behind רבי אלעזר הקפר on the road. He found a ring with a דרקון figure on it. He met a young גוי and said nothing to him. Then he met an adult גוי and told him: cancel its status. The גוי did not, so he slapped him, and the גוי cancelled it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a found ring with a דרקון figure. The story sets up three laws that the גמרא will learn from it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A found דרקון ring is forbidden, but a גוי can cancel its status through ביטול. The details matter: רבי אלעזר הקפר skipped the child, chose an adult, and forced him when he refused. Each detail will become a law.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Hana said
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Once I was walking

phrases.aramaic: אַחַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר בְּרִיבִּי בַּדֶּרֶךְ,
phrases.english: behind Rabbi Elazar HaKappar the distinguished on the road,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָצָא שָׁם טַבַּעַת וְעָלֶיהָ צוּרַת דְּרָקוֹן,
phrases.english: and he found a ring there with a dragon figure on it.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָצָא גּוֹי קָטָן וְלָא אָמַר לוֹ כְּלוּם,
phrases.english: He met a young gentile and said nothing to him.

phrases.aramaic: מָצָא גּוֹי גָּדוֹל וְאָמַר לוֹ: בַּטְּלָהּ,
phrases.english: He met an adult gentile and said to him: Cancel it.
He did not cancel it, so he slapped him, and he cancelled it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the דרקון figure with a real case of finding one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A found דרקון ring was made permitted when an adult גוי cancelled its status, even though he was forced to.

steps.title: Three laws learned from the story
steps.stepSummary: From the story the גמרא learns three laws: a גוי can cancel another's idol, only someone who understands עבודה זרה can cancel it, and a גוי's cancellation works even when forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this: A גוי can cancel his own עבודה זרה and his friend's. Someone who understands עבודה זרה and its accessories can cancel it, but someone who does not understand them cannot. And a גוי can cancel it even against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws three laws from the details of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ring was not the adult גוי's, yet he could cancel it, so a גוי can cancel someone else's idol. רבי אלעזר הקפר skipped the child, so only someone who understands עבודה זרה can cancel. The slap worked, so even a forced cancellation counts.

keyTerms.meaning: its accessories, items used in its worship

steps.whatToRemember: Three laws of ביטול: a גוי can cancel someone else's idol, only someone who understands עבודה זרה can cancel it (so not a child), and forced cancellation still works.
steps.whyThisMatters: These three rules set who can permit a found idolatrous object, which is the practical point of this whole section.

phrases.english: Learn three things from it:
Learn from it that a gentile can cancel
his own idol and that of his fellow.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ יוֹדֵעַ בְּטִיב שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
phrases.english: And learn from it that one who understands the nature of idol worship
and its accessories can cancel it,
but one who does not understand the nature of idol worship
and its accessories cannot cancel it.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ גּוֹי מְבַטֵּל בְּעַל כׇּרְחוֹ.
phrases.english: And learn from it that a gentile can cancel it even against his will.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws legal rules from the details of the story in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A גוי who understands עבודה זרה can cancel its status, even someone else's idol and even under force. A child cannot.

steps.title: רבי חנינא asks why a cancellation was needed if the owner gave up
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא challenges the story: a lost object's owner gives up on it (יאוש), so the ring should already have lost its idol status without any גוי canceling it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא mocked this. He asked: Doesn't רבי אלעזר הקפר accept what we learned? Someone who rescues things from a lion, a bear, a cheetah, a troop of soldiers, a river, the sea's tide, or a flooding river, or someone who finds things on a main road, in a big plaza, or anywhere many people pass, may keep them. That is because the owners give up on them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא attacks the story from step 10. He argues that a ring lost in a public place was already given up by its owner, so having a גוי cancel it was pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted source teaches that in these situations the owner gives up hope, and the item becomes the finder's. רבי חנינא reasons that once the idol-worshipping owner gave up on the ring, it should automatically stop being his idol. That would make רבי אלעזר הקפר's request to the גוי unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: ridiculed, mocked; here it means sharply challenged
a title of honor, "the distinguished one"
the owner giving up hope of getting his lost item back
main road and large public plaza

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina mocked this,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הַקַּפָּר בְּרִיבִּי
phrases.english: and doesn't Rabbi Elazar HaKappar the distinguished hold
that which we learned:
One who rescues things from a lion or from a bear
or from a cheetah or from a troop of soldiers
or from a river or from the tide of the sea
or from the flooding of a river,
and one who finds something on a main road or in a large plaza,
or anywhere that many people pass —
these things belong to him,
because the owners give up hope of them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְגַדֵּף בַּהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא, וְלֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story's assumption that the ring needed an active cancellation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר הקפר's action of having a גוי cancel the found ring
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lost item in a public place is given up by its owner, so the idol status should end automatically and no cancellation is needed.

steps.title: אביי: giving up the item is not giving up its worship
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the owner gives up on owning the ring but not on its being worshipped, because he assumes whoever finds it will end up worshipping it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: True, the owner gives up on getting the item back. But does he give up on its forbidden status? He tells himself: If a גוי finds it, he will worship it. If a Jew finds it, it is valuable, so he will sell it to a גוי, who will worship it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends רבי אלעזר הקפר. He explains that the owner's giving up does not remove the ring's idol status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי splits giving up into two parts: giving up on owning the object, and giving up on it as an idol. The owner expects the ring to keep being worshipped by whoever ends up with it. So it never stopped being an idol, and a real cancellation by a גוי was still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: "granted that...", admitting one point before arguing another
the forbidden status, here meaning its status as an idol

steps.whatToRemember: An owner can give up on a lost idol without giving up on its idol status. That is why רבי אלעזר הקפר still needed a גוי to cancel it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Granted that he gives up on the item itself,
does he give up on its forbidden status?
He says to himself:
If a gentile finds it —
he will surely worship it,
if a Jew finds it —
since it is worth a lot of money
he will sell it to a gentile, and he will worship it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נְהִי דְּמִינַּהּ מִיָּיאַשׁ, מֵאִיסּוּרָא מִי מִיָּיאַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי חנינא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: giving up ownership versus giving up idol status
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Giving up on the lost ring would automatically end its idol status.
steps.terutzMaskana: The owner expects the ring to keep being worshipped, so its idol status remains until a גוי cancels it.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's pictures of the moon
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: רבן גמליאל kept pictures of the moon's shapes on a wall tablet and used them to question simple witnesses about the new moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: רבן גמליאל had pictures of moon shapes on a tablet on the wall of his attic. He showed them to ordinary people and asked them: Did you see one like this, or like this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting a משנה about רבן גמליאל's moon diagrams. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses who came to report seeing the new moon could not always describe it well. רבן גמליאל used drawings to help them say what they saw. Making a picture of the moon is the detail the גמרא will question next.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" is a משנה in ראש השנה 24a.

phrases.english: Pictures of the shapes of the moon
Rabban Gamliel had in his attic,
on a tablet on the wall,
with which he would show the ordinary people,
phrases.notes: These are witnesses who came to say they saw the new moon.

phrases.english: and he would say to them:
Did you see one like this, or did you see one like this?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: דְּמוּת צוּרוֹת לְבָנוֹת הָיָה לוֹ לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion, still connected to the theme of forbidden images.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל kept drawings of the moon's shapes to question witnesses.

steps.title: How could he make pictures of the moon?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבן גמליאל: the פסוק "לא תעשון אתי" forbids making images of ה׳'s attendants, such as the moon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that allowed? It is written: "You shall not make with Me," which means: do not make images of My attendants who serve before Me!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבן גמליאל was allowed to make pictures of the moon. It quotes a פסוק that seems to forbid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "לא תעשון אתי" is read as forbidding images of the heavenly beings that serve ה׳, which includes the sun and the moon. רבן גמליאל's moon pictures seem to break that rule. The answer will come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: My attendants, the heavenly bodies that serve ה׳

phrases.english: And is it permitted?
But isn't it written: "You shall not make with Me,"
meaning, do not make the likeness of My attendants
who serve before Me!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל making pictures of the moon
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids making images of the heavenly attendants, and the moon is one of them.

steps.title: אביי: Only things that can truly be copied are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the תורה only forbade making copies of attendants that can really be reproduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The תורה only forbade copying those attendants that it is possible to make exactly like.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge from "לא תעשון אתי" against רבן גמליאל's moon pictures. He narrows what the איסור covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that any image of ה׳'s attendants, the moon included, is forbidden. אביי says the איסור only covers things a person can actually make a true copy of. The moon in the sky cannot really be copied, so רבן גמליאל's pictures are not the forbidden kind.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible to make something exactly like them

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The Torah only forbade [copying] attendants
that it is possible to make exactly like them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא שַׁמָּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 against רבן גמליאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the איסור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any image of ה׳'s attendants, including the moon, is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only attendants that can truly be reproduced are forbidden, so pictures of the moon are allowed.

steps.title: A ברייתא: no exact copies of the בית המקדש or its vessels
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids building exact copies of the parts of the בית המקדש and its table and מנורה, but allows a מנורה with a different number of branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: A person may not build a house shaped like the Sanctuary, a porch shaped like the Entrance Hall, a courtyard shaped like the Temple courtyard, a table shaped like the Table, or a מנורה shaped like the מנורה. But he may make one with five, six or eight branches. One with seven he may not make, even from other kinds of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support אביי's rule. It lists exact copies of the בית המקדש and its vessels that a person may not make.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything on the list is something a person can really build: a building, a table, a מנורה. Only an exact copy is forbidden, which is why a מנורה with five, six or eight branches is allowed. This matches אביי: the איסור is about copies that can truly be made.

keyTerms.meaning: Shape or design; an exact model
The Sanctuary building in the בית המקדש
A porch, a roofed area open on the sides
The Entrance Hall in front of the היכל
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
The seven-branched lamp of the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think every מנורה is forbidden. Only a seven-branched one, the exact design of the בית המקדש's מנורה, is forbidden. Five, six or eight branches are fine.

phrases.english: As it is taught [in a baraita]:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בַּיִת תַּבְנִית הֵיכָל,
phrases.english: A person may not make a house in the shape of the Sanctuary,
a porch in the shape of the Entrance Hall,
a courtyard in the shape of the Temple courtyard,
a table in the shape of the Table,
a menorah in the shape of the Menorah.
But he may make

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל חָמֵשׁ וְשֶׁל שֵׁשׁ וְשֶׁל שְׁמוֹנֶה,
phrases.english: one of five, or of six, or of eight [branches],
but one of seven he may not make,
even of other kinds of metal.
phrases.notes: A מנורה for the בית המקדש can also be made from metals other than gold, so a seven-branched one is still a real copy.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא: לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה אָדָם בַּיִת תַּבְנִית הֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support אביי's rule from step 16.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that only things that can truly be copied are forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding exact copies of the בית המקדש, its table and its מנורה, while allowing a מנורה with a different number of branches.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר יהודה: Not even a wooden מנורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה adds that a seven-branched מנורה is forbidden even if made of wood, since the חשמונאים made one that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: Even one of wood he may not make, the way the חשמונאים made it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with the view of רבי יוסי בר יהודה. He adds wood to the forbidden materials.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the ברייתא forbade a seven-branched מנורה from any metal. רבי יוסי בר יהודה goes further: wood is forbidden too. His reason is that the חשמונאים made the בית המקדש's מנורה from wood, which would mean a wooden one is a real copy.

keyTerms.meaning: The חשמונאים, the family of kohanim who ruled and rededicated the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
Even one of wood he may not make,
in the way that the Hasmoneans made it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף שֶׁל עֵץ לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a stricter opinion about wood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seven-branched מנורה may not be made even from wood, based on what the חשמונאים did.

steps.title: The חכמים reject the proof from the חשמונאים
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the חשמונאים never used wood: they used iron spits covered with tin, and later upgraded to silver and then gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Is that your proof? They were iron spits, and they covered them with tin. When they grew rich, they made them of silver. When they grew richer still, they made them of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבי יוסי בר יהודה. They say his proof from the חשמונאים doesn't hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's proof depends on the חשמונאים having made the מנורה from wood. The חכמים say it was actually iron spits covered with tin, so it was metal, not wood. As they became wealthier they upgraded to silver and then gold. So there is no proof that a wooden מנורה is a real copy.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that a proof? (a way of rejecting a proof)

steps.whatToRemember: So far, אביי's rule is that the איסור of "לא תעשון אתי" only covers exact copies of things that can truly be made, like the בית המקדש and its vessels. On that basis, רבן גמליאל's moon pictures would be allowed. The next step challenges this rule.

phrases.english: They said to him: Is that a proof?
They were spits of iron,
and they covered them with tin.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets, 'and they covered them,' is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: When they grew rich, they made them of silver.
When they grew richer again, they made them of gold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יוסי בר יהודה's proof from the חשמונאים in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the חשמונאים that a wooden מנורה counts as a copy.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The חשמונאים never made the מנורה from wood. It was iron covered with tin, then silver, then gold.

steps.title: Are images of attendants that cannot be copied really allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי's distinction using a ברייתא that forbids making images of ה׳'s attendants on high.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really allowed to make images of attendants that cannot truly be copied? But a ברייתא teaches that "You shall not make with Me" means: do not make images of My attendants who serve before Me on high!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's answer from Step 16 by quoting a ברייתא that seems to forbid images of exactly the kind of attendants אביי would allow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From אביי's answer it follows that attendants which cannot really be reproduced may be pictured. But the ברייתא says the פסוק forbids images of the attendants who serve ה׳ 'on high', and those are attendants we cannot truly copy. So the ברייתא seems to contradict what follows from אביי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Attendants: the things that 'serve' ה׳, like the sun, moon, stars and angels
It is impossible to make copies of them
Is it permitted? Here it is a challenge, not a simple question

steps.confusionAlert: אביי never said outright that hard-to-copy attendants are permitted. The גמרא is drawing that out from his rule, which forbade only the attendants that can be copied.

phrases.english: And attendants that it is impossible to make copies of
phrases.notes: This follows from אביי's answer in Step 16: if only copiable attendants are forbidden, the others would seem allowed.

phrases.english: is it permitted?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
"You shall not make with Me"
You shall not make the likeness of My attendants
who serve before Me on high!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשַׁמָּשִׁין שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּמוֹתָן מִי שְׁרֵי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about the מנורה in Steps 17-19, the גמרא returns to challenge אביי's distinction from Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that only attendants which can truly be reproduced are forbidden to copy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From אביי's rule it follows that hard-to-copy attendants are allowed. But a ברייתא forbids images of the heavenly attendants, which cannot truly be copied, so the ברייתא contradicts that result.

steps.title: אביי begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces אביי, who will answer the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup: it tells us that אביי is about to answer the challenge. His actual answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening words of the answer appear here. The content of אביי's reply, which will explain how the ברייתא fits with his rule, follows in the coming lines.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the reply to the challenge in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Not yet given here; only the opening of אביי's answer appears.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to forbid images of the heavenly attendants, which cannot be copied, against what follows from אביי's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Still to come. אביי's explanation follows in the next lines.
